column4: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ opens an oath by entities identified through retreating motion, another close instance of the section's unnamed oath-subjects disclosed by what they do.
الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ identifies the oath-subjects as coursing and disappearing; their running both echoes the 100:1 runners and meets the horses hidden behind the veil in 38:32.
أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ makes acquisitive increase distract the human, a direct development of the section's intense attachment to property.
حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ carries distraction by increase straight to the graves, the same abrupt passage from love of wealth to opened graves in surah 100.
The wealth-gatherer thinks أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ; this ayah contributes the delusion attached to the gathering named in 104:2.
نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ joins the wealth-gatherer's fate to kindled fire, a specific meeting of the section's property attachment and its ignition image.
الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ carries that fire into human hearts, joining the wealth scene to the section's eventual exposure of what lies inside the chest.
كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ commands precisely the self-opposing witness that the section reads in the human's testimony against himself.
وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ says excuses cannot displace the self-knowledge stated in 75:14, clarifying the force of the human's adverse testimony.
Whether people hide what is in their breasts or disclose it, God knows it; this directly parallels the section's chest as a temporary container whose contents will be brought out.
The remembered covenant and وَقُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا are followed by God's knowledge of breasts, joining pledged service to the inward reality that will test it.
Within a battle encounter, the enemy is shown as few and God is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ; the gathered-force setting and inward knowledge meet two distinct details of the section.
وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ makes loved wealth something the righteous give, rather than the terminus of the human's intense attachment.
Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's way enact the section's misdirected love of property and prepare the bodily fire scene in 9:35.

Hoarded wealth is heated in hellfire and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs; the ayah specifically joins property, fire, and the body, images the section holds together around the horse-human comparison.

نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ establishes Solomon as an excellent, returning servant before the horses appear, materially informing the two possible relations between horse-love and remembrance of his Lord.
Immediately after decorated desires including horses, the ayah asks whether it should announce what is better and locates the enduring reward عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ.
الْمَالُ وَالْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا names property as worldly adornment, then prefers enduring righteous deeds; it supplies the boundary for the decorated horses and wealth of 3:14.
Worldly life is adornment, boasting, and rivalry in wealth before it withers; this reverses the apparent durability promised by intense love of valuable property.
فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ commands movement toward remembrance and away from trade, a direct ethical reorientation of both running and property-love.
When people see trade or amusement they disperse toward it and leave the messenger standing; bodily movement toward gain realizes the danger opened by Solomon's horse-love in relation to remembrance.
The breast opened to submission is opposed to a breast made constricted and tight; the human chest carries guidance or refusal, unlike the horse's chest whose exertion is outwardly evident.
A breast opened to submission and light from its Lord is set against hardened hearts, specifying the inward human condition hidden within the ṣadr.
The sky أَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ listens to its Lord as it undergoes its assigned act, the creation-level counterpart to the horse giving itself to an owner and the human failing his Lord.
The earth likewise listens to its Lord and is bound to do so, repeating the obedience that throws the section's human ingratitude into relief.
The lamp's oil nearly gives light وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ; fire almost appearing without contact forms a precise boundary against the runner's contact-made sparks.
وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ states that wealth cannot serve its owner at his fall, opposing the animal body that does serve its owner with the property the human trusts.
The ayah contrasts the believers' love with concealed hatred and closes with God's knowledge of breasts, making the chest the place where an outward relationship's contrary truth resides.
وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ repeats the direct formulation that the contents of human breasts are already known before their final extraction.
Every human's record is fastened to him and brought out as an open book; it supplies the personal evidence that allows 17:14 to make the human his own accountant.
إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ describes people massed against the believers; faith grows before a threatening gathered force of the kind entered in 100:5.
وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَّمًّا gives a concrete acquisitive act immediately before the intense love of wealth in 89:20.
أَنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ repeats the warning that valued possessions test the human's relation to God.
وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا uses khayr for what the human receives and withholds, a specific character parallel to the possessiveness heard in love of khayr.
لَا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنسَانُ مِن دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ joins al-insan to an untiring appetite for khayr; the sense is broader than wealth, but the persistence sharpens the section's diagnosis of attachment.
